item.title: 【農業】 Homestead food production improves women’s dietary diversity in Bangladesh
item.description: Nature Food, Published online: 12 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s43016-026-01353-w Empirical evidence on the contribution of different pathways through which homestead food production programmes may improve women’s dietary diversity remains scarce. In Bangladesh, garden production and nutrition education were found to be critical.

item.title: 【農業】 Impact pathways of a homestead food production programme on women’s dietary diversity in Bangladesh
item.description: Nature Food, Published online: 12 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s43016-026-01354-9 The contribution of homestead food production (HFP) to nutrition and dietary diversity is context-specific and involves multiple pathways. Using panel data on 2,612 women in 96 settlements in rural Bangladesh, this study identifies and measures the impact pathways of a 3-year HFP intervention.

item.title: 【農業】 Integrated bundled measures could halve reactive nitrogen losses and reach net-zero greenhouse gas emissions in global livestock systems
item.description: Nature Food, Published online: 11 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s43016-026-01352-x A meta-analysis of ~3,000 empirical observations shows that systemic shifts in manure management and technology integration can reduce reactive nitrogen and carbon dioxide emissions from global livestock systems under various mitigation scenarios.

item.title: 【農業】 Granular datasets will be key to predicting the impact of food system transitions on micronutrient status in China
item.description: Nature Food, Published online: 08 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s43016-026-01358-5 Models of China’s food supply suggest that expanding plant-based production could improve micronutrient availability. More granular data on food composition, nutrient bioavailability and population micronutrient status are essential to validate these models and inform food policy in China.

item.title: 【環境】 Understanding and reducing the intention–behaviour gap in climate action
item.description: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 13 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02630-z Climate-friendly intentions do not always translate into action. This Review synthesizes evidence on the intrapersonal, social and structural mechanisms underlying this gap and outlines interventions that offer actionable strategies to close it.

item.title: 【環境】 Increasing atmospheric dryness and storms accelerates biomass turnover in Amazonian forests
item.description: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 13 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02639-4 The carbon sink of tropical forests is in part constrained by biomass turnover. This study assesses aboveground biomass turnover in the Amazon and finds that convective storms are the main driver of spatial variation in turnover and future climate impacts will lead to accelerated biomass turnover.

item.title: 【環境】 Exporting environmental harm
item.description: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 12 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02582-4 Multinational investment is vital for African growth, yet it drives higher rates of forest loss than local industry. Researchers now suggest that home-country laws should hold global firms accountable for their environmental footprint abroad.

item.title: 【環境】 The environmental impact of multinational firms in Africa
item.description: Nature Climate Change, Published online: 12 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41558-026-02637-6 Developing countries are faced with trade-offs where multinational corporations could help local economic growth, but also cause more environmental damage than domestic counterparts. This research confirms such negative effects and discusses how better governance could reduce detrimental outcomes.

item.title: 【環境】 Hierarchical materials from fused silk
item.description: Nature Sustainability, Published online: 12 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01821-y Natural silk, mechanically strong and biodegradable, offers great potential for sustainable functional materials. Here the authors present a simple thermomechanical method for fabricating high-performance structural and optically active materials directly from silk fibres.

item.title: 【環境】 3D-printed multiscale-ordered hierarchical frameworks for rapid atmospheric water harvesting
item.description: Nature Sustainability, Published online: 12 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01834-7 Atmospheric water harvesting provides a vital pathway for mitigating freshwater scarcity. This study introduces a 3D-printed porous structure designed for rapid water capture, overcoming a critical bottleneck that has long hindered the large-scale deployment of atmospheric water harvesting technology.

item.title: 【環境】 Sweet spots for nitrogen reduction in a coastal watershed
item.description: Nature Sustainability, Published online: 12 May 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01828-5 Coastal nitrogen pollution is a critical sustainability challenge with environmental, social and economic consequences. Upstream ‘sweet spots’ where interventions will have maximum mitigation effectiveness and social buy-in are attractive but may prove difficult to implement in urban stream networks.
